name: Azul
metaDescription: Free Azul score calculator for 2–4 players. Add your score track to the end bonuses for complete rows, columns and colours and find the winner instantly.
intro: In Azul most points are scored as you tile your wall, but the end-of-game bonuses can still swing the result. Enter each player's score track and their completed rows, columns and colours to get the final ranking.

categories.label: Score track
categories.help: Your score on the scoring track after the last round of wall-tiling, with floor line penalties already taken off.

categories.label: Complete horizontal rows
categories.help: Rows of 5 tiles across your wall.

categories.label: Complete vertical columns
categories.help: Columns of 5 tiles down your wall.

categories.label: Complete colours
categories.help: Colours with all 5 tiles placed on your wall.

tiebreaker: If players are tied, the one with the most complete horizontal rows wins. If they are still tied, they share the victory.

rules.heading: How scoring works in Azul
body: The game ends at the end of the round in which at least one player completes a horizontal row of 5 tiles on their wall. After the final wall-tiling, each player adds end-of-game bonuses to the score already on the scoring track.

rules.heading: Scoring during the game
body: Each tile you move to your wall scores straight away. A tile with no neighbours scores 1 point. If it joins a horizontal line of tiles, it scores 1 for each tile in that line; if it joins a vertical line, it scores 1 for each tile in that line. If it joins both, both lines score.
Tiles left on your floor line cost points at the end of each round: −1, −1, −2, −2, −2, −3, −3 for the first to seventh spaces. Your score cannot go below zero.

rules.heading: End-of-game bonuses
body: Each complete horizontal row of 5 tiles is worth 2 points. Each complete vertical column of 5 tiles is worth 7 points. Each colour for which you placed all 5 tiles on your wall is worth 10 points.
Columns and colours are worth far more than rows, which is why experienced players often keep playing for them even when the game is about to end.

faq.q: What are the end-game bonuses in Azul?
faq.a: 2 points per complete row, 7 points per complete column and 10 points per colour with all 5 tiles placed.

faq.q: Can your Azul score go negative?
faq.a: No. Floor line penalties can drop your score to zero but not below.

faq.q: How are ties broken in Azul?
faq.a: The tied player with more complete horizontal rows wins. If still tied, the victory is shared.
